issues.legal_issue: A pending proceeding challenging an order declaring land surplus abates after the repeal takes effect when the State has not taken possession of the land.
material_facts: An authority declared land surplus, and the challenge to that order remained pending in appeals before the Court.
The repeal had taken effect in the State before the Court decided the appeals.
The record did not indicate that the State had taken possession of the surplus land; the appellant maintained that possession remained with it, and the State filed no reply on possession.
issues.conclusion: The proceedings abated because the record did not indicate that the State had taken possession of the surplus land.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4 of the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Repeal Act, 1999 provides that proceedings relating to an order under the principal Act that are pending when the Repeal Act commences abate. Its proviso excludes specified proceedings relating to Sections 11, 12, 13 and 14 of the principal Act to the extent they concern land whose possession has been taken by the State or an authorized person. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: pending_challenge_to_surplus_order and repeal_in_force and not state_possession_taken

predicates.pending_challenge_to_surplus_order: A challenge to an order declaring land surplus remained pending before a court or other authority.
predicates.repeal_in_force: The repeal of the law governing the surplus-land order had taken effect in the relevant state.
predicates.state_possession_taken: The State or a person authorized by it had taken possession of the land.
predicates.proceeding_abates: The pending proceeding ends by abatement.

issues.definition: When a challenge to a surplus-land order is pending, the repeal is in force, and the State has not taken possession, the proceeding abates.
